cluster_summary: This cluster comprises vulnerabilities in Jenkins where authorization checks are missing or incorrectly scoped, authorization logic is bypassed due to flawed assumptions, sensitive data is exposed through serialization of full user objects, and CSRF protection is missing on GET endpoints. These issues allow unauthorized access to sensitive information and state-changing actions.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add explicit permission checks (e.g., checkPermission, hasPermission) at the entry point of each method..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Missing permission check on API endpoints
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Add explicit permission checks (e.g., checkPermission, hasPermission) at the entry point of each method.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add explicit permission checks (e.g., checkPermission, hasPermission) at the entry point of each method.
sub_patterns.name: Missing permission check on API endpoints
sub_patterns.root_cause: Methods exposed via API or endpoints do not verify the caller's required permission before returning data or executing actions.
